top.title: Matos accepts Swansea fans' anger over shock exit
top.description: Vitor Matos was due to celebrate a year in charge at Swansea next Tuesday [AFP via Getty Images] Vitor Matos admits he knows why Swansea City fans will be angry following his sudden departure from the club. The Portuguese head coach quit the Championship side this week for the top job at French League 1 club RC Strasbourg. His move took Swansea by complete surprise, just a week before marking his first year in charge with the club sixth in the table and having signed a new contract until 2030 in July. Speaking at his first press conference at Strasbourg, Matos admitted he does not "expect any goodwill" from the Welsh club's supporters. He said: "One situation I need to address is Swansea. It was a really hard and tough decision to leave the club mainly because from the first day, they treated me with all respect and care – me and my family. "So it was a really tough decision to leave and that's why I needed to thank everyone there. "Saying that, I really don't expect any good will from the Swansea supporters after my decision. I understand they are angry with that, but it's a club that I love that I worked every day to make better, me and my staff." Listen: Ashley Williams' first press conference back at Swansea A badly timed shock - the story of Matos' Swans exit Listen to the latest Swansea City news Swansea are expecting a compensation package of about £5m and have appointed former players Ashley Williams, Leon Britton, Joe Allen and Kris O'Leary to take temporary charge before Saturday's league fixture against West Bromwich Albion. "To the staff and to the players I have no doubt they will succeed in the future," said Matos. "I have no doubt that the manager will go into the office and make the club move forward and fulfill the dreams of the club." He added: "I'm really proud to be Racing's next manager. This is a wonderful club that deserves all thee respect of everyone."

top.title: Nebraska Has One Final Chance to Change the Recruiting Narrative Against Ohio State
top.description: Trae Taylor headlines a group of 19 recruits expected in Lincoln as Nebraska looks to deliver a statement victory in its final home game of the season. Nebraska’s final home game against Ohio State carries significance far beyond the result on Saturday afternoon. For the seniors, it represents an emotional farewell to Memorial Stadium. For the coaching staff, it is another opportunity to demonstrate that the program is heading in the right direction. And for the 19 recruits expected in Lincoln, it is a chance to see whether Nebraska can finally turn its promise into results against one of college football’s heavyweight programs. There is no getting around the fact that this has been a frustrating season for the Huskers. Nebraska has shown enough to suggest that the gap between itself and the Big Ten’s elite is narrowing, but competing with those programs and actually beating them are two very different things. With the 2027 recruiting class shaping up to be one of Nebraska’s strongest in recent memory, Saturday represents another important opportunity to reinforce the belief that Matt Rhule is building something special in Lincoln. Trae Taylor’s Return Is a Massive Positive Perhaps the most encouraging name on the visitor list is five-star quarterback commit Trae Taylor. Taylor has become the centrepiece of Nebraska’s 2027 recruiting class, both through his ability on the field and his leadership off it. His return to Lincoln is particularly significant given the uncertainty surrounding Nebraska’s offense. The Huskers have struggled to find consistency offensively, and the firing of offensive coordinator Dana Holgorsen has raised legitimate questions about the direction of the unit. For a five-star quarterback, the identity of the offensive coordinator, the system he will operate in and the development opportunities available are understandably important considerations. Taylor would be well within his rights to seek reassurance about Nebraska’s offensive future. Instead, his continued involvement with the program is an encouraging indication that his commitment extends beyond any single coach. Taylor has also played an important role in bringing Nebraska’s 2027 recruiting class together. The relationships he has developed with fellow commitments could prove invaluable as the Huskers approach another potentially turbulent offseason. He will be joined by seven other 2027 commits, including four-star safeties Tory Pittman III and Corey Hadley Jr. The presence of such a significant group of committed players provides an opportunity for Nebraska to reinforce those relationships while allowing the recruits to spend valuable time together. Keeping this class intact must be one of the coaching staff’s biggest priorities. top.description: (Photo by Todd Kirkland/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders head to play at the Denver Broncos on Sunday. Kickoff is set for 1:25 p.m. PT. Here are three things to know about the Broncos: They’re rolling: The 7-2 Broncos have won five straight games. They’re struggling on the ground: The Broncos aren’t running the ball well. They are averaging 81.4 yards a game on the ground and just 3.7 yards per carry. Bo Nix gets hot when he has to: Denver quarterback Bo Nix isn’t perfect, but he gets hot when the game is on the line. top.title: Why Miami QB Darian Mensah Wasn’t A 2026 Johnny Unitas Golden Arm Award Finalist Over Arch Manning
top.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The 2026 Johnny Unitas Golden Arm Award finalists were announced on Friday, with many of the nation’s top quarterbacks in the mix for the honor. However, there was one major surprise for college football fans with the Miami Hurricanes ‘ Darian Mensah kept off in favor of the Texas Longhorns ‘ Arch Manning. No one could argue against the inclusions of CJ Carr ( Notre Dame Fighting Irish ), Devon Dampier ( Utah Utes ) and Drew Mestemaker ( Oklahoma State Cowboys ). All three quarterbacks had resumes and numbers worthy of being recognized as the nation’s best upperclassman quarterback in college football. However, the difference in stats between Mensah and Manning are staggering. Read More: Best College Football Defenses Right Now ESPN QBR Pass Yards /YPG TD – INT YPA Darian Mensah 88.6 (1st in CFB) 3,076 / 308.6 29 (9.1%) – 2 (0.6%) 9.7 Arch Manning 62.3 (63rd) 2,198 / 219.8 19 (6.6%) – 10 (3.5%) 7.6 Mensah has statistically been the best quarterback in college football this season, averaging the most passing yards per game (307.6) among the Johnny Unitas Golden Arm Award finalists while ranking fourth nationally in passing touchdown rate, third in yards per attempt (9.7) and first in ESPN QBR (88.6). Both statistically and based on record (9-1 vs. 9-2), he should be ahead of Manning. At a time when there’s a growing belief among fans and even college football analysts that the College Football Playoff rankings are heavily biased toward SEC teams, this seemed like another example of conference favoritism. So, why isn’t Mensah a Golden Arm finalist? Because under the criteria set forth by the Golden Arm Foundation , a quarterback is ineligible from consideration if they’ve transferred twice. Mensah started for the Tulane Green Wave in 2024 before transferring to become a star with the Duke Blue Devils this past season. By transferring a second time to replace Carson Beck as the Hurricanes’ quarterback in 2026, he made himself ineligible for the Johnny Unitas Golden Arm Award. It certainly feels like an outdated criterion given the state of modern college football, but it could also be a non-issue in the years to come if the NCAA and Power Four conferences have their way with changes to transfer rules. For now, Mensah is ineligible, and Manning inexplicably made the list despite being an average starting quarterback this season. Read more at Sportsnaut

top.title: Detroit Lions name a new captain on defense
top.description: Nov 8, 2026; Miami Gardens, Florida, USA; Detroit Lions safety Chuck Clark (36) runs with the ball after an interception during the second half against the Miami Dolphins at Hard Rock Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect As first reported by Justin Rogers and confirmed by coach Dan Campbell on Friday, the Detroit Lions have a new defensive captain. Veteran safety Chuck Clark was given the honors earlier this week, after the Lions had lost two defensive captains to injury over the past three weeks: Jack Campbell (neck), Aidan Hutchinson (knee). “It felt like the right thing to do,” Campbell said. “We obviously lost a couple of our captains. He’s really just filled the void as the season has gone on. Type of guy he is, it just speaks for itself. And he’s just grown inside this locker room, he’s a great teammate, and he’s just got leadership qualities through the room. Communication is outstanding. His production has gone up as the season’s gone up. Everybody’s got a lot of faith in Chuck. He’s just kinda one of those bell-cow guys for us right now. So he earned that, so proud of him.” Clark is in his 10th NFL season and first with the Lions. Campbell noted that they knew about Clark’s leadership qualities before they signed him to a one-year, $1.5 million deal this offseason, but you never know for sure until he’s actually in the building. Thus far, he’s lived up to his reputation. “You get around him and you see it first hand. There’s nothing fake about it. He’s just real,” Campbell said. “He’s one of those guys that people gravitate to him. He’s just got it. He’s a great communicator, same guy every day, very consistent, smart, grinder. He’s everything you really want in that type of role.” In addition to his leadership, Clark has become an important part of the gameday lineup. He’s been a steadying force in Detroit’s ever-shifting secondary, logging more defensive snaps (540) than anyone else on the team. And while his role may soon decrease with the return of Brian Branch a few weeks ago and Kerby Joseph this week, Campbell noted that they want to still use all of their safeties, Clark included. “Everybody’ got a role. We’re trying to use everybody that we can in that defensive room. So all those safeties? We want to use them,” Campbell said. “There’s a role for all of those guys. And now you get Kerby back in the fold. So we’ve got a couple of things that we can do here and have flexibility to do.”

top.title: Russia is developing a nuclear space weapon, US intelligence report finds
top.description: null Last month, the U.S. Defense Intelligence Agency (DIA) released a chilling and info-packed report judging the scope and breadth of threats posed by the nation's adversaries in space. The new report focuses on China , Russia and the emerging space powers of Iran and North Korea. It looks at what's happening in Earth orbit and beyond, including cislunar space, the region between our planet and the moon . The report — the 2026 edition of "Challenges to Security in Space" — is the third iteration of the DIA's unclassified intelligence assessment on space-related challenges and threats to U.S. national security, as well as the extent to which space is treated internationally as a warfighting domain . Information within the report, which you can read here , is current as of July 2026. DIA's mission is to provide intelligence on foreign militaries to help prevent wars, and win the ones that are fought. Up-front finding The report's up-front finding is that China, Russia, Iran, and North Korea are developing, testing, deploying and using space capabilities "in a way that threatens the security of all space systems and their associated space benefits." Indeed, China and Russia are developing "a formidable spectrum" of offensive capabilities to degrade or destroy space services of other countries, from kinetic destruction to sophisticated jamming and cyber operations. The DIA report also notes that "the production of cheaper, smaller, and simpler satellites , which are faster to develop and deploy, along with the expansion of commercially available launch services, are driving the rapid integration of commercial space alternatives to support national security." While space commercialization is making previously government-centered space services widely available to interested parties, the DIA report adds, that availability also includes state and non-state actors with malign interests. There are a range of threats to space-based services, both commercial and military. Some are reversible, while others are not. (Image credit: DIA) Counterspace worries A major item dealt with by the DIA is "counterspace" — and it's not the kind that you'll find in your kitchen. Counterspace operations can be either offensive or defensive. They can be used on purpose to reversibly or irreversibly deny, disrupt, degrade, damage or destroy a space object or component of a space system. Here are the key elements of counterspace, as identified within the DIA report: Antisatellite (ASAT) missiles are designed to kinetically strike and destroy satellites. ASAT missiles could produce massive amounts of debris that can remain in orbit for decades or even centuries. Physical or cyberattacks against ground sites and other terrestrial infrastructure supporting space operations can also threaten satellite services. top.title: NFL Predictions: Bears offense primed for a big day against Saints
top.description: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - OCTOBER 19: Caleb Williams #18 of the Chicago Bears passes the ball during the second half of the NFL football game against the New Orleans Saints at Solider Field on October 19, 2025 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images When the initial spread dropped for the Chicago Bears and the New Orleans Saints, I thought, that’s a really big number . Four days ago, the 7-2 Bears opened as a 9.5-point favorite over the 3-6 Saints; it then climbed to 10.5 later that evening. It’s currently up to 11.5 (at the time I’m writing this), according to FanDuel Sportsbook , but the more I look at this matchup, the more I think the Bears will easily cover. The Bears are coming off their bye week, so they’ll be well rested and ready to make another statement. I’m not saying get ready for a 59-point explosion like Week 1, but a 50-burger wouldn’t surprise me. The running game has been criticized lately, but did you realize it still ranks number 1 in attempts and is 4th in yards per game? The Bears have a top-10 offense by most metrics while the Saints have a bottom-10 defense. On the flip side, New Orleans’ offense has been bottom-10, while the surprising Bears have been top-10 on defense. And that’s with Jeffery Simmons only being a Bear for two games. Chicago’s offense is what everyone thinks of when discussing how well-timed their bye week was, but the defense also gets a chance to self-scout and figure out how best to play off Simmons. I like the Bears’ offense starting strong on Sunday, their defense getting a few turnovers, and them winning 38 to 17. top.title: 2026 Atlanta Braves Player Review: Elieser Hernández
top.description: ATLANTA, GA - JULY 31: Elieser Hernández #57 of the Atlanta Braves pitches in the seventh inning during the game against the Washington Nationals at Truist Park on July 31, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Matthew Grimes Jr./Atlanta Braves/Getty Images) | Getty Images One of the more interesting mini-plots of the 2026 Atlanta Braves season was Elieser Hernández’s journey up and down, and all around, the Gwinnett Express. He’d come up, pitch some big innings, get designated for assignment shortly afterwards, return to Gwinnett, and do it all over again at some point down the road. It’s time to examine how this journey went for him. How Acquired Hernández inked a minor league deal with the Braves last November and began the season with the Gwinnett Stripers in Triple-A. It took Hernández all the way until late July for the Braves to call him up to the bigs and boy, did he end up coming through in a big spot for Atlanta. What were the expectations? For the first five years of his career, Hernández was an up-and-down arm with the Marlins. He did make 48 starts, 42 relief appearances, and log over 280 innings, but they came with a -0.7 fWAR. Things weren’t much better in 2024 as the Brewers and Dodgers took a brief flier on him, but he ended up pitching in Korea with the LG Twins for part of that season, as well as 2025. All that meant was that when the Braves added him back to an MLB organization after the 2025 season, the expectations were that he would provide depth for Gwinnett, with no real assumption of any kind of usefulness or quality if anyone bothered to call him up to the bigs. 2026 Results But, the Braves did call him up! Hernández pitched in his first big league game since 2024 on July 24, which is when Walt Weiss called his name in the seventh inning of a game where the Braves were trailing the Orioles by one run. Hernández then proceeded to face 13 batters and ended up clearing three innings as a result, which helped get the Braves into extra innings and eventually ended up earning him the pitcher win after the Braves broke out for four runs in the tenth inning of that one. This was a fantastic result for Hernández and his reward was getting designated for assignment and eventually electing free agency before returning to the Braves organization by July 28. He did give up one run on five hits this time around, but he struck out four batters along the way and the Braves cruised to victory thanks to his efforts. top.title: Divisional Rankings: Ciryl Gane is UFC’s defending champion, but is he MMA’s true No. 1 heavyweight?
top.description: Ciryl Gane was triumphant at UFC 334 | Jeff Bottari, Zuffa LLC In the ever-shifting MMA landscape, ranking the world’s greatest fighters might seem like a fool’s errand, but that’s exactly what we’ve set out to do with the MMA Fighting Global Rankings. Here, our esteemed panel sorts out the movers and shakers from every division to provide you with the most definitive list of the best fighters on the planet. It’s official: Ciryl Gane is not only the UFC’s undisputed heavyweight champion, he’s a defending one as well. But how undisputed is he, really? Gane’s curious rise to the top of the division is well-documented. In his second shot at the undisputed title, Gane faced off with Tom Aspinall at UFC 321, but the duel ended inconclusively after Gane poked Aspinall in the eyes, rendering him unable to continue. With Aspinall having to undergo surgery for the resulting injuries, Gane was booked to fight Alex Pereira in an interim heavyweight championship bout at UFC White House in a matchup presumably made to give Pereira the opportunity to become the UFC’s first-ever three-division titleholder. History was put on hold as Gane defeated Pereira by second-round knockout ( a result that wasn’t without controversy, at least according to “Poatan” ) to become interim champion a second time. Then, in September, with no firm date for Aspinall’s return on the horizon, Gane was promoted to undisputed status and promptly booked to fight Josh Hokit in the main event of UFC 334. Gane took care of business this past Saturday, withstanding a relentless assault from Hokit to convincingly out-strike him and claim a unanimous decision victory. So he’s the clear-cut No. 1 heavyweight, right? Not so fast. As it stands, the MMA Fighting Rankings panel still has Aspinall hanging on to the No. 1 spot, though the vote was not unanimous. Aspinall and Gane both received two first-place votes each, with lineal champion Francis Ngannou claiming one as well. Let’s not forget Ngannou holds a win over Gane from their championship fight back in 2022, and Gane’s case is also hurt by lackluster performances against Jon Jones and Alexander Volkov in recent years. That said, Ngannou’s most recent win is against UFC washout Philipe Lins, and Aspinall will be subject to our 18-months of inactivity automatic removal rule if he does not return to action by April. So Gane could soon by No. 1 by default, which as we all know is the sexiest way to become recognized as the best in your field. top.description: (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images Flip on a Sacramento Kings broadcast and you’re likely to be inundated with graphics, statistical queries or fun facts framing Darius Acuff Jr. in an illustrious ensemble. Names like Michael Jordan, LeBron James, Oscar Robertson and Luka Dončić are frequently mentioned alongside the rookie guard, who is averaging a robust 26.2 points, seven assists (3.9 turnovers) and 3.6 rebounds through the first 14 games of his career. It’s an esteemed neighborhood for Acuff to reside in and certainly an encouraging omen as he progresses further into his NBA tenure. Skeptics, however, will peek beyond the box score and point to Sacramento’s 1-13 record, Acuff’s relative scoring inefficiency (53.3% true shooting, 24th percentile, per Dunks & Threes) or his ball-dominant tendencies to downplay his raw production. They’ll note how much of the Kings’ 27th-ranked offense is channeled through him and posit his true impact pales in comparison to those All-Star-level statlines by citing a host of metrics and data. Stretching back to his sensational freshman season at Arkansas a year ago, Acuff has divided the masses with his play. The first month of his rookie campaign has done little to assuage that polarization, a reality existing independent of anything he’s responsible for but rather captures the cantankerous discourse enveloping the sports world more than ever these days. Nonetheless, there is plenty to examine, praise and critique about Acuff’s first 14 games. He’s flashed loads of promise and indicated various areas of concern as the Kings presumably build around him moving forward. So, what about his skill-set may suggest future stardom and what may offer reasons for worry in an NBA ecosystem increasingly cruel and unforgiving to smaller guards? Let’s take a look. Every star player needs a superpower. Some are more consequential or prominent than others but they all have one. There are a horde of guards who can haphazardly dribble the air out of the ball. But Acuff makes it immensely practical. As the league continues to evolve and grow sharper fangs defensively while also upsizing its offensive hubs, dribbling — especially inside the arc or against pressure — is a bit of a lost art. top.description: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - MAY 23: Cole Young #2 of the Seattle Mariners is tagged out while trying to reach third base by Maikel Garcia #11 of the Kansas City Royals during the game at Kauffman Stadium on May 23, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. You can read all about the details and early analysis of the trade here and here . However, today’s post is meant to get y’all contemplating your orbs and looking into the future to see how this trade shakes out five years down the road or more. Let’s prognosticate! Here are some prompts to answer in the comments: Who ends their career with higher WAR: Bryce Miller or Maikel Garcia? Does Logan Evans become the underrated gem in this trade by having a breakout season for Kansas City in 2027 or even 2028? How will losing Ferrer effect the Mariners bullpen? Are Miller’s struggles mental, physical, both, or neither? Assuming full health or close to it, what is Garcia’s slash line for the Mariners in 2027? And how many stolen bases? As much as it pains me to give up on Bryce Miller when there is still a chance he puts together the kind of season that had me picking him as my dark horse Cy Young candidate before the 2o25 season, bringing in a Real Life Third Baseman who can also hit a bit does fill me with optimism. If Miller ends up an ace in KC, I’ll be happy for Cowboy Bryce, but hopefully the revamped infield defense is enough to overlook the regret of seeing Miller put it all together for another team. What do y’all think? Let’s hear your answers to the prompts in the comments, plus any other trade hot takes you want to share.

top.title: Friday Discussion: What does the hiring of Trev Alberts mean for Michigan Football?
top.description: COLLEGE STATION, TEXAS - JULY 2:Texas A&M athletic director Trev Alberts speaks during Michael Earleys welcome ceremony on Tuesday, July 2, 2024, in College Station. Earley was appointed head coach of Texas A&Ms baseball program on Sunday, June 30. (Ishika Samant/Houston Chronicle via Getty Images) The University of Michigan has a new Athletic Director, as Trev Alberts has been widely reported to be accepting the role. Alberts is the current Texas A&M Athletic Director and has previously been at Nebraska both as a player and Athletic Director. Widely regarded as a relatively ruthless AD, Alberts is sure to bring widespread changes to Michigan athletics for as long as he’s here. Today’s discussion question is this: how will Alberts’ hiring affect Michigan football specifically? There are a few ways you can take this. Let’s start with the elephant in the room: Kyle Whittingham’s employment. It’s no secret that Whittingham is firmly on the hot seat thanks to a combination of the team’s record, his press conference performance, and his handling of the offense or lack thereof. Prior to the hiring of Alberts, the prevailing wisdom was that Whittingham likely wouldn’t be fired because there was no one in a position to do the actual firing. With the new university president not yet in place and Warde Manuel nearing the end of a lame-duck tenure, it would have taken the Board of Regents and/or a conglomeration of donors to find a way to make moves behind the scenes. All of that is thankfully out the window now as Trev Alberts’ first task on the job will likely be evaluating Kyle Whittingham and the football staff. You have to think that this is bad news for Whittingham. Not only does Michigan now have someone in place to make a firing if appropriate, but they also clearly placed an emphasis on making the hire quickly so that a move could be made. If the university didn’t intend to make a change, why else would they expedite the hiring of an AD and make the hire now? The timing seems far too convenient. Alberts also has a reputation for being ruthless. He has ruffled feathers at both Nebraska and Texas A&M by firing quite a few long-time staff members. Trev has also taken a “spend first, figure out how to pay for it later” approach. Buyouts such as Jason Beck’s and Kyle Whittingham’s certainly won’t make Alberts balk. However, certain traditions may also be at risk as Alberts will enforce his will throughout the department. There’s no doubt that Alberts is a proverbial mover-and-shaker in the college football world. He will without a doubt be the most noteworthy AD at Michigan in the past few decades. Whether that’s a good thing or a bad thing is yet to be seen. Michigan has won national championships in both football and men’s basketball in the last three years, yet somehow a departmental shake-up feels necessary. top.title: Yankees Birthday of the Day: Clark Griffith
top.description: 1913 Washington Senators: Manager Clark Griffith. (photo by: HUM Images/ Universal Images Group via Getty Images) Though Clark Griffith is the first man to manage the New York baseball team we now call the Yankees, his time in New York is merely one chapter in a story of one of the giants of baseball’s early history. That’s no shot at Griffith’s time in New York and his importance to the franchise. It’s just he had such an amazing life and career. He was already an accomplished hurler when he came to New York and became the player-manager of the club, in its first season in The Big Apple. And long after he hung up his cleats, he remained an integral part of baseball in the first half of the 20th century. Clark Calvin Griffith Born: November 20, 1869 (Clear Creek, MO) Died: October 27, 1955 (Washington, DC) Yankees Tenure: 1903-07 (player/manager), 1908 (manager) Clark Griffith was already a grizzled veteran when American League President Ban Johnson named him manager of the New York Highlanders (often called the Americans in the press) prior to the 1903 season. It was the inaugural campaign for the club, which relocated from Baltimore after the Orioles folded following two seasons. The diminutive Griffith (listed at 5-foot-6) was a right-handed pitcher, and a good one, at that. Between 1894 and 1901, he won at least 20 games in a season seven times. His first season in New York was also his last one as a starting pitcher, and he tossed more than 200 innings while managing the club to a disappointing fourth-place finish. Griffith’s pitching days were not over, however. He transitioned to the bullpen and continued to pitch at a high level while trying to steer the Highlanders to a pennant. In 1904 and 1906, he came close, with the club finishing in second place each season, mere games from wining the American League. Modern Yankee fans are used to skipper Aaron Boone getting himself tossed from games, though he was shockingly well-behaved in 2026. He’s far from the first Yankee manager to get the hook, of course. Griffith, by virtue of being the first manager, gets that honor. Like his modern successor, Griffith also got himself suspended for his conduct toward umpires. On Monday, August 27th, 1906, Griffith took umbrage with a safe call at first base while playing St. Louis. As a result, the umpires ordered Griffith off the field. The Highlanders’ skipper took his sweet time about it. Unfortunately for him, AL President Johnson was in the crowd, and the next day he suspended Griffith indefinitely. Yeesh. “Savages in the Box,” this was not. Seems a little harsh. But wait — there’s more. The indefinite suspension might have something to do with Griffith fighting umpire Tim Hurst earlier in the season, which also got him suspended. For that round of fisticuffs, Griffith received a five-day suspension. His ban in August lasted a week. The Highlanders bottomed out on Griffith’s watch in 1908, and in June he decided it was time for him to move on. Owner

nigeria.description: Warsaw and its allies said Friday that a Russian missile landing in Poland was a “provocation” from Moscow as thousands of European troops were holding exercises nearby. Poland said two Russian missiles hit its territory early on Friday, landing in southeastern Poland as drills were due to take place. Nobody was hurt, Poland said. Authorities said one Kh-101 missile was confirmed to have landed in the eastern village of Nowy Lipowiec. A second missile is suspected to have hit another location and a jet-powered drone a third. The projectiles crossed into the NATO country as Russia pounded neighbouring Ukraine and thousands of European troops were holding unprecedented army drills in southeastern Poland. Several European defence ministers were in Poland for the drills. Prime Minister Donald Tusk said everything pointed to the fact that these were not accidental stray missiles. “Three Russian objects violated Polish airspace. They fell on Polish land. One exploded. There is no destruction, no casualties,” he said, adding: “This is not just my opinion but of our foreign partners and NATO: this does not look like a coincidence.” He said he believed the incident was linked to the European drills. “We are dealing with an intentional provocation,” he added. He said the objects “fell close” to where “armies of the Coalition of the Willing” were training in Nowa Deba, southeastern Poland. “Coalition of the Willing” refers to a group of Ukraine’s European backers who are prepared to send peacekeeping troops to the country. Nowy Lipowiec, where the first missile fell, is a 1.5-hour drive from where the drills are taking place. Just a day before the incident, US media outlet Fox News quoted Donald Trump as saying Russian leader Vladimir Putin “has been landing drones in Poland, and a couple of little missiles, by mistake”. Tusk said on Friday that Poland would give the United States access to the missile debris. “I don’t always agree with the interpretation of the US side on these incidents. We are cooperating with the Americans. They have access to the places, to the debris of the objects.” The Kremlin has not yet commented. Senator Akpabio gave the charge in Abuja on Friday at the inauguration of “Tinubu Again Movement” a grassroots mobilization movement, convened by the Minister of State for Defence, Dr Bello Matawalle, aimed at securing more than 20 million votes for the re-election of President Bola Tinubu in 2027. In a statement signed by the Special Assistant on Media/Communication to the President of the Senate, Anietie Ekong, Akpabio urged the APC members and supporters not to be distracted by the antics of the opposition parties who aimed to attract sympathy by inciting violence in the run up to the election. The President of the Senate said: “Please be careful. Don’t allow them to provoke you to violence. Because they know they are losing, they will sponsor some misguided youths to throw stones at you. If they throw stones at you, your target is to garner votes and defeat them. “By January 16, 2027, they will know the difference between stones and votes. When you are certain of winning you don’t deploy stones and violence as your weapons but you persuade them with the monumental achievement of the APC administration.” Akpabio charged the members of Tinubu Again Movement to carry the message of the Renewed Hope administration to their various polling units, wards and local government areas to sensitize the populace on the achievement of the administration of President Tinubu. nigeria.title: Russia pummels Ukraine, missile hits Poland, after Putin threat
nigeria.description: Moscow pounded Ukraine with massive strikes Friday, with Kyiv saying at least seven people were killed in the capital, while neighbouring Poland accused Moscow of “provocation” after two Russian missiles likely landed in the southeast corner of the NATO country. Russia’s Vladimir Putin had vowed a “painful” response to Kyiv’s strikes on Moscow’s Crimea bridge after holding a summit with China’s Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump. Ukraine’s Volodymyr Zelensky called the night-time strikes one of Moscow’s largest of the nearly five-year war, denouncing what he said was Russian “terror”. Zelensky, who met allies in Berlin Thursday, said Putin’s attempts to “redraw the world” with Xi and Trump had been a “failure”. In China, Putin said he “shared responsibility” for global peace with Xi and Trump and issued a “declaration toward peace” that made no mention of Moscow’s invasion of Ukraine. AFP journalists saw people hunkered down in Kyiv’s metro stations, which double as overnight air-raid shelters, sleeping on yoga mats, camping chairs and in pop-up tents. Kateryna Liubychenko, 32, took her toddler down to try to get some sleep through the bombardment. “It’s painful to have to stop our child from living,” she told AFP. Two people were killed in Lviv, power was knocked out in swathes of the country and in Kyiv, three vital transport bridges were hit, officials said. Explosions rang out through the night as Ukrainian officials reported more than 80 missiles and 400 drones were fired. Three bridges that cross the Dnipro river were hit, Mayor Vitali Klitschko said, threatening yet more disruption to daily life in the city. France requested a UN Security Council meeting over the strikes, saying “Russia will have to answer for its actions there”. Poland decries ‘provocation’ In neighbouring Poland, authorities said one missile was confirmed to have landed in the eastern village of Nowy Lipowiec, with another missile and a jet-powered drone suspected to have hit two other locations. Warsaw said no-one was hurt. Prime Minister Donald Tusk said the weapons flying into Poland were deliberate. “The provocation may have been linked with the fact that there are (military) exercises taking place on the territory of Poland,” Tusk told a televised press conference in Warsaw. Thousands of European troops are taking part in military exercises in southeastern Poland. “Nobody can say that this was an innocent coincidence,” Tusk said, adding he had informed NATO “straight away”. Tusk said that NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte would be in Warsaw on Saturday and that he would inform him of the incident. Poland is one of five countries Europe picked to represent it at future US-led talks on Ukraine. nigeria.title: Viral Video: Military uniforms found with bandits not from us – DHQ
nigeria.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The Defence headquarters has denied supplying military camouflage uniforms allegedly found in the possession of suspected bandits in a viral social media video, insisting that the clothing did not originate from the Nigerian military. Read Also: Viral Video: ‘We recovered 12 AK-47 rifles, kidnap victims’ – Military defends engagement with bandits The footage, circulating widely online, showed large quantities of woodland and desert camouflage uniforms spread on the ground, Several others were packed in sacks and allegedly held by suspected bandits. Reacting to the video, the Director of Defence Media Operations, Maj. Gen. Michael Onoja ruled out the possibility that the uniforms were supplied by the military. “That is not possible,” he said, when asked whether the clothing originated from the Nigerian military. Onoja also dismissed suggestions that the uniforms might have been stolen from military supply vehicles attacked by bandits, saying no such incident had been reported. “No such report has been made. It is not from the Nigerian military,” he added. The video reportedly showed two different camouflage patterns, identified as woodland and desert designs, raising renewed concerns over the circulation of military clothing among criminal groups and unauthorised persons. The development comes amid longstanding concerns about criminals, impersonating security personnel to perpetrate attacks, kidnappings and other crimes. In February 2024, the Federal Government reiterated restrictions on the unauthorised use of military camouflage by civilians, warning against the misuse of security uniforms and equipment by criminal elements Minister of State for Defence, Bello Matawalle had stated that the restrictions were necessary to enable security agencies to distinguish legitimate personnel from impostors. He noted that criminals had exploited military and other security agencies’ uniforms to deceive members of the public and facilitate criminal activities. The government’s position was aimed at curbing impersonation, preventing the misuse of military uniforms and strengthening security operations across the country. nigeria.title: Boat capsizes with 300 passengers in Bayelsa
nigeria.description: By Samuel Oyadongha, Yenagoa A tragedy struck the riverine enclave of Southern Ijaw Local Government Area on Friday, as a cargo boat conveying over 300 passengers capsized, leaving many feared dead. The ill-fated vessel was reportedly en route to Ukubie community from Anyama Ijaw, when the incident occurred at 12 noon. According to preliminary reports, the boat, which was heavily overloaded with passengers traveling for a burial ceremony, went down in the waterways between Oweikorogha and Angiama communities. Eyewitness accounts indicate that the tragedy might have been averted. It was learned that some passengers had suggested the boat stop at Oweikorogha to decongest the vessel, but the advice was allegedly ignored. The boat reportedly capsized shortly after departing the community. While the actual casualty figure remains unconfirmed, fears are mounting that the death toll could be substantial given the number of persons on board. Mr. Ipigansi Igoniba, Chairman of the State Maritime Workers Union, confirmed the incident to our correspondent but stated that information regarding the disaster was still hazy. “I cannot give the casualty figure right now. We have sent our members to the scene of the accident and search and rescue efforts for the missing persons are ongoing,” Igoniba said. Rescue operations are currently underway, though independent confirmation of the number of survivors or fatalities is yet to be established. The incident has cast a pall of mourning over the community, highlighting once again the dangers of overcrowding and unsafe travel on the state’s waterways. nigeria.title: MultiChoice cuts entry-level DStv, GOtv subscriptions to ₦6,000
nigeria.description: MultiChoice Nigeria has introduced restructured DStv and GOtv subscription packages, with entry-level options starting at ₦6,000, following customer feedback on affordability and content preferences. The company’s Chief Executive Officer, Kemi Omotosho, disclosed this during an interview on the Global Business Report on ARISE News on Friday, saying the new packages were designed to simplify subscription choices and provide customers with access to entertainment, sports and other content. She said the company had listened to its subscribers and adjusted its offerings to better address their needs. “We recognised that our customers are dear to us, so we listened to our customers, we simplified our offerings,” she said. Under the new arrangement, DStv subscribers can choose from four packages: Starter, Select, Sports and Premium, while GOtv offers Easy, Starter, Select and Sports. Omotosho said the Starter package, which costs ₦6,000, provides access to more than 90 channels, including Africa Magic Plus, the Premier League Match of the Week, selected UEFA Champions League matches and La Liga coverage. She also explained that the Sports package had been redesigned from the former Compact offering to provide broader access to major sporting competitions. According to her, the package includes all Premier League and Champions League matches, as well as UFC and WWE content, alongside channels available on the Starter and Select packages. Clarifying the subscription rates, Omotosho said the Sports package costs ₦21,000 for new subscribers, while the ₦19,000 rate applies only to existing Compact subscribers migrating to the new package. “When you move into the new pack, it’s ₦21,000 on the Sports pack,” she said. The CEO also highlighted the benefits of MultiChoice Nigeria’s integration into the Canal+ Group, which operates in more than 70 countries across Africa, Asia and Europe. She said the integration had strengthened the company’s capacity in content acquisition, technology and partnerships while retaining its focus on the Nigerian market. “We’re basically riding on global muscle, but we still want to be very relevant to the Nigerian consumer,” she stated. On the company’s transition towards digital entertainment, Omotosho said MultiChoice regarded satellite television and streaming services as complementary platforms rather than competing products. “For us, streaming is not an ‘either/or,’ it is ‘and’,” she said. She cited DStv Stream, which enables subscribers to access television content online without a satellite dish or decoder. According to her, the company’s technology-agnostic approach allows customers to choose satellite television for reliability in areas with limited broadband access or streaming services for greater flexibility. nigeria.title: AI-generated fake content threatens democracy, national security – Okonkwo
nigeria.description: By Dickson Omobola Executive Chairman of United Nigeria Airlines, Professor Obiora Okonkwo, has expressed concerns over the growing sophistication of artificial intelligence, AI, saying its capacity to generate convincing fake images, videos and voices poses fresh threats to democracy, national security and public trust, particularly during elections. Okonkwo warned that hate speech, misinformation and irresponsible communication could be as destructive as weapons, saying the 1994 Rwandan genocide was an example of how manipulated information could incite mass violence, destroy lives and destabilise nations. He spoke while delivering the opening address at the African session of the World Public Relations Forum, WPRF, Abuja 2026, where he challenged journalists, public relations practitioners, advertisers and corporate communication professionals to strengthen self-regulation and uphold ethical standards to prevent communication platforms from becoming instruments of propaganda and social division. Speaking on the theme, ‘Responsible Communication in Africa: The Importance of Self-Regulation and Information and Media Literacy,’ he said the influence of communication demanded greater responsibility from those who shaped public opinion. He said: “The lesson is unmistakable. Communication is not always an innocent exercise. In the hands of irresponsible actors, the microphone can become as disruptive as a very dangerous weapon.” He said the 2023 general elections were an example of the dangers of irresponsible communication, adding that although social media facilitated political mobilisation, it also enabled the circulation of fabricated election results, unverified claims and divisive ethnic and political narratives. He recalled that the European Union Election Observation Mission documented misleading political communication during the polls, warning that such practices could undermine public confidence in democratic institutions and citizens’ ability to make informed electoral choices. He said: “In an age of unprecedented information flow, the credibility, integrity and social value of what we communicate are as important as the freedom and the platforms through which we communicate.” The airline chairman also cited the COVID-19 pandemic, when the World Health Organisation identified an infodemic of false and misleading information that confused populations, encouraged risky behaviour and weakened confidence in public health institutions. He said misinformation surrounding Ebola outbreaks in parts of the Democratic Republic of Congo similarly fuelled distrust of health workers and undermined disease-control interventions. “These examples demonstrate that irresponsible communication can threaten not only democratic stability but also human lives,” he warned. nigeria.title: ASUU Suspends Taraba Varsity Strike After Gov Kefas’ Intervention
nigeria.description: The Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU), Taraba State University chapter, has conditionally suspended its ongoing strike. The union resolved to suspend the total, comprehensive and indefinite strike, which began on 12 October 2026, with effect from 20 November 2026, following Governor Agbu Kefas’ approval of the full implementation of the 2025 agreement between the Federal Government and ASUU. The decision was reached at a congress held on Friday to determine the union’s position on the governor’s appeal for the suspension of the industrial action and his approval of the agreement’s implementation. This was contained in a statement issued by the ASUU chairman at Taraba State University, Garba Mbave. ASUU-TSU had embarked on the strike over the Taraba State Government’s failure to implement the 2025 Federal Government-ASUU remuneration agreement and pay outstanding salary arrears accrued from January 2026. The union had earlier engaged the state government on the demands, but commenced the indefinite industrial action on October 12 after efforts to resolve the dispute failed. A file photo of Governor of Taraba State Agbu Kefas. Photo: Facebook/Agbu Kefas The union expressed profound appreciation to Kefas, the Commissioner for Tertiary Education, the Head of Service and the university management for their interventions, constructive engagement and commitment towards resolving the industrial dispute. The union also appreciated members of the public, students, parents, staff and the entire university community for their patience, understanding, solidarity and cooperation throughout the strike. “The support, restraint and confidence demonstrated during this challenging period are highly appreciated. The Union acknowledges the sacrifices and inconveniences occasioned by the strike and appeals for continued understanding and cooperation as efforts towards the restoration of normal academic activities and sustainable industrial harmony are pursued,” the statement said. ASUU Logo ASUU reaffirmed its commitment to industrial harmony, constructive dialogue and the restoration of normal academic activities, while stressing the need for the faithful implementation of the resolutions reached. It urged the Taraba State Government, the university management and all relevant parties to demonstrate good faith by ensuring the full and timely implementation of the resolutions contained in the communiqué and the Memorandum of Action (MoA). “The sustainability of industrial harmony and the uninterrupted academic calendar depend on mutual trust, accountability and strict adherence to agreed commitments. “Accordingly, all parties are urged to honour their respective obligations to prevent a recurrence of the dispute and safeguard the interests of staff, students, the University and the wider education sector,” the statement added. nigeria.title: United Nigeria Airlines begins Jos flights to Lagos, Kano, Owerri
nigeria.description: United Nigeria Airlines will commence scheduled flight operations from Jos to Lagos, Kano and Owerri on November 24 and 29, 2026, providing residents of Plateau State with additional air connections to other parts of the country. The airline said tickets for the new routes were already available for purchase. The Lagos–Jos–Lagos route will operate four times weekly on Tuesdays, Wednesdays, Fridays and Sundays, while the Jos–Kano–Jos and Jos–Owerri–Jos routes will each operate twice weekly. Flights between Jos and Kano will operate on Tuesdays and Fridays, while those between Jos and Owerri will run on Wednesdays and Sundays. However, because the Owerri airport is currently closed, operations on the Jos–Owerri route will commence on Sunday, November 29, five days after the initial launch date. The development follows the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between the Plateau State Government and United Nigeria Airlines on Monday, November 9, at the office of the Commissioner for Transport, Jatau Gyang, in Jos. Under the agreement, the airline will introduce scheduled services on the Jos–Kano and Jos–Owerri routes, which the state government said were previously not served. Speaking after the signing, Gyang said the partnership was part of the state government’s broader efforts to position Plateau as a leading destination for investment, tourism, commerce and economic opportunities. He commended the airline’s management for its confidence in the state’s vision. According to him, the Jos–Owerri route will ease movement between Plateau and the South-East and South-South regions, thereby supporting trade, investment, tourism and social exchanges. He said the Jos–Kano connection would further strengthen Plateau’s relationship with the North-West, which he described as home to major commercial and industrial centres offering opportunities for business partnerships and trade. Responding on behalf of the airline, its Managing Director, Mazi Osita Okonkwo, said the agreement was significant because it would connect the South-East, South-West and North-Central regions. He described Plateau as a strategic state and assured that the airline would maintain its service standards. Okonkwo also commended Governor Caleb Mutfwang for his vision and strategic direction, while acknowledging Gyang’s efforts in facilitating the agreement. Passengers can book flights through the airline’s website, mobile application or accredited travel agents. The NUC had declared the institution’s operations in Nigeria illegal, alleging that it was admitting students, running academic programmes and claiming to award degrees through unauthorised campuses and learning centres across the country. However, the university has challenged the commission’s position, insisting that its legal existence as a foreign institution is distinct from the regulatory status of its learning support centres in Nigeria. In a public notice issued on Tuesday, the NUC’s Director of Public Affairs, Rita Okonjo, said the institution, also known as the University of America, had not been authorised to operate or award degrees in Nigeria. She identified the centres allegedly linked to the institution as Cosmopolitan International Business School (CIBS), Garki, Abuja; its purported Federal Capital Territory learning centre; and the University of America College of Science and Technology, also known as UAPOLY, Ekpoma, Edo State. Okonjo said the commission’s investigations showed that the institution was not accredited by any agency recognised by the United States Department of Education or the Council for Higher Education Accreditation (CHEA). She explained that its purported listing in the Integrated Postsecondary Education Data System (IPEDS), as well as claimed registrations in California and Florida, did not constitute accreditation or authorisation to award recognised university degrees. The NUC spokesperson also dismissed claims that the institution had obtained approval from the Federal Ministry of Education, the Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board, the National Board for Technical Education and the Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria. According to her, even if such approvals had been obtained, they would not confer the authority to operate a university or award degrees in Nigeria. nigeria.title: Fountain of Life denies closure amid leadership crisis
nigeria.description: By OLAYINKA LATONA LAGOS — The Fountain of Life Church has denied reports that its premises have been sealed, insisting that the church remains open, although access to its facilities is currently restricted amid an ongoing leadership dispute. The church, in a post on its official Instagram page, shared a graphic bearing the inscription, “DON’T BELIEVE THE NOISE! CHURCH IS NOT SEALED,” while inviting worshippers to attend its Sunday service. The clarification comes amid a leadership crisis involving Pastor Jimmy Odukoya and the church’s board, which has generated public attention in recent days. However, a visit by Vanguard correspondents to the church premises revealed restricted access, with activities appearing limited. There was no visible presence of police personnel at the premises, while private security operatives were stationed at the entrance. Efforts by a Vanguard reporter to gain access to the church were unsuccessful, as a security official said only persons with official business within the premises would be allowed in. The restricted access comes despite the church’s public invitation to worshippers to attend Sunday’s service. The church had earlier announced the postponement of its 2026 Thanksgiving Service, initially scheduled for Sunday, November 22, stating that a new date would be communicated. The developments come against the backdrop of a legal battle over the church’s leadership. The Lagos State High Court had restrained Odukoya from holding himself out as Senior Pastor and Spiritual Head of the church following an application by the church’s Incorporated Trustees. Justice O.O. Adewunmi-Oshin granted the interim orders on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, in a suit filed by the trustees. The court also restrained Odukoya, whether acting personally or through proxies, from interfering with, disrupting or obstructing the church’s activities, governance and other operations. The orders were granted ex parte, meaning they were made without first hearing Odukoya’s response to the application. However, the court preserved his right to apply to set aside the orders or respond to the substantive claims after being served with the court processes. The case was adjourned until December 1, 2026, for mention. The leadership dispute became public on November 17, when a faction of the church’s Board of Trustees announced that it no longer recognised Odukoya as senior pastor, citing a succession video reportedly recorded by the late founder, Pastor Taiwo Odukoya, in December 2021. The trustees subsequently named Pastor Rotimi Okpaise as interim spiritual and administrative leader. However, Odukoya and the church leadership rejected the decision, maintaining that his appointment as senior pastor in September 2023 was valid. nigeria.title: Gunmen attack, machete former Super Eagles captain Odegbami
nigeria.description: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta ABEOKUTA — Former Super Eagles captain and football administrator, Chief Segun Odegbami, has sustained injuries following an attack by three armed men at his residence in Abeokuta, Ogun State. The incident reportedly occurred at about 2:30 a.m. on Friday at his residence in the Ibara Government Reservation Area (GRA). Sources in the neighbourhood said the attackers allegedly overpowered members of his domestic staff and driver before gaining access to his bedroom, where he was attacked with machetes. Odegbami, 74, is the proprietor of Eagles 7 Sports Radio 103.7 FM and a former captain of Nigeria’s national football team. A resident, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said the attackers initially asked to see the former international but were told by his domestic staff that he was not at home. The source said the attackers reportedly became suspicious after noticing that the generator was running, suggesting that someone was inside the residence. According to the resident, the assailants allegedly assaulted the domestic staff before making their way into Odegbami’s bedroom, where they attacked him. The source added that Odegbami reportedly resisted the attackers during the incident, forcing them to flee the residence. He was subsequently taken to an undisclosed hospital for medical attention. The incident was reported to the police, although the motive behind the attack had yet to be established. Meanwhile, the Ogun State Commissioner of Police, Bode Ojajuni, has visited Odegbami to sympathise with him and assure him of the command’s commitment to investigating the incident. In a statement issued by the command’s spokesperson, DSP Oluseyi Babaseyi, the commissioner said he had ordered an immediate and thorough investigation to identify and apprehend those responsible. Ojajuni also wished the former football international a speedy recovery and assured him that the police were treating the incident seriously. The police confirmed that Odegbami had been discharged from the hospital, adding that investigative efforts were ongoing to establish the circumstances surrounding the attack and bring those responsible to justice. The commissioner urged members of the public to remain calm and provide credible information that could assist the investigation through established police communication channels. nigeria.title: European leaders urge Russia to halt winter energy attacks
nigeria.description: …Back ceasefire, security guarantees for Ukraine By Favour Ulebor, Abuja Germany, France, the United Kingdom and Ukraine have called on Russia to suspend attacks on energy facilities throughout the winter, describing an energy truce as a first step towards ending hostilities in Ukraine. The leaders also called for a ceasefire to facilitate food exports through the Black Sea, stressing that safe passage for ships was critical to global food security. The position was contained in a joint statement shared by the German Embassy in Nigeria on Friday, following a meeting in Berlin on Thursday involving Ukraine, the United States and members of the Coalition of the Willing, a group of countries supporting Ukraine. The leaders condemned what they described as an escalation in Russian missile and drone attacks against Ukrainian civilians and civilian infrastructure, while expressing condolences to the families of victims. They reaffirmed their solidarity with Ukraine and its right to defend itself against Russia’s invasion, insisting that continued attacks would not weaken their support for Kyiv. The statement said the countries would work with other partners to provide Ukraine with additional missile defence systems before winter, particularly those capable of intercepting ballistic missiles to protect civilians and critical infrastructure. The leaders also backed direct talks between Ukraine and Russia, with the participation of the United States and European countries, and welcomed Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy’s willingness to accept an immediate ceasefire and engage in meaningful negotiations. They, however, insisted that any peace agreement must respect Ukraine’s territorial integrity, sovereignty and right to determine its security arrangements and alliances. According to the statement, proposals concerning the European Union or NATO would require the consent of their respective members. The leaders further called for legally binding security guarantees for Ukraine once a ceasefire takes effect. The proposed arrangements include a US-led mechanism to monitor and verify the ceasefire and a European-led multinational force supported by the United States. Other measures could include continued military, financial and technical assistance to Ukraine, as well as a legally binding commitment, subject to national procedures, to take steps to restore peace and security if Russia launches another armed attack. On military assistance, the leaders reaffirmed a pledge by NATO allies to provide €70 billion in military equipment, assistance and training in 2026, with at least the same level of support in 2027. They also said the European Union’s Ukraine Support Loan would provide €90 billion in military and financial assistance by the end of 2027. business.title: Researchers Publish Security Analysis of Bitcoin’s Post-Quantum SHRINCS Proposal
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Researchers Publish Security Analysis of Bitcoin’s Post-Quantum SHRINCS Proposal Several researchers have published a 131-page security analysis of SHRINCS, a proposed post-quantum signature scheme for Bitcoin, and are asking the wider community to look for flaws in it. Researcher Mikhail Kudinov announced the first version Thursday in a thread on X, saying the paper reduces SHRINCS’ security to the properties of its underlying hash function. The analysis, dated Nov. 18, estimates classical security of 121.4 to 122.7 bits for SHRINCS, though those figures rest on assumptions that include three unproven conjectures. Kudinov said the work is not finished. The team is still working on a new analysis of a property called SM-DSPR, whose bound has so far been conjectured, and on tightening a reprogramming step and improving a bound against quantum attackers. How SHRINCS works SHRINCS is a hash-based scheme, meaning its security rests on hash functions rather than the elliptic curve math behind today’s Bitcoin signatures. It places two designs under one key: a stateful part built on FXMSS with WOTS+C, and a stateless fallback built on SLH-DSA. Because both use the same hash function, Kudinov said, the proof has to cover both. Signature size is the main cost. Under the draft proposal, stateful SHRINCS signatures run from 548 to 4,619 bytes, while the stateless fallback is 5,777 bytes. Schnorr signatures on Bitcoin today are 64 bytes, and ECDSA signatures typically come in around 71. Signatures take up scarce block space, so larger ones mean fewer transactions per block. The risk of a stateful signature The compact stateful path carries a danger. It relies on one-time keys, and if a wallet accidentally reuses one, an attacker can forge a signature for that address and steal the funds. Wallet software therefore has to track the state of every key. The stateless path avoids the problem, but at a much larger size. Jonas Nick, Blockstream’s director of research, told Isabel Foxen Duke, head of the MARA Foundation, on MARA Foundation TV that wallets must automatically fall back to the stateless path whenever a state counter could be compromised. “It needs to be impossible for the user to behave in a way that this catastrophic event happens,” he said. “Wallet developers need to deal with this stateful component correctly.” Nick also warned that heavy use of the larger signatures would weigh on the network. “We don’t know what the fee market will look like once we have these very big signatures,” he said. “And it’s not just the fee market, it’s also just fewer transactions fit into a block, meaning fewer people can use Bitcoin. And I think this changes the value proposition of Bitcoin.” Researchers ask for review The authors are clear that the analysis needs scrutiny. business.title: Block Says Most Bitcoin Payments on Square Are for Coffee and Food
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Block Says Most Bitcoin Payments on Square Are for Coffee and Food Most bitcoin payments at Square sellers are small, everyday purchases at coffee shops and restaurants, Block said in a new report that it hopes will inform a debate in Congress over a tax break for small crypto purchases. The report, “The State of Bitcoin Payments,” covers completed bitcoin payments at U.S. Square sellers from Nov. 1, 2025, to Oct. 15, 2026. The median payment was about $13, and the average was about $29. Food and drink businesses took 72% of those payments, Block found. That is a bigger share than the category’s 67.5% slice of regular card payments on Square over the same period. “Most bitcoin payments are small and routine,” the company wrote on X Thursday, calling the report one of the first datasets on how people spend bitcoin in the local economy. Coffee, quick bites and repeat visits Coffee shops and fast food businesses accounted for 62.6% of the bitcoin payments in the food and drink category, with a median payment of $9.10. Grocery stores made up a smaller share but had the highest average payment in the group, at $60.73. Small tickets dominated. About 42% of bitcoin payments on Square were under $10, and 65.1% were under $20. Those sub-$20 payments made up just 19.1% of total payment value, though, with a few larger purchases accounting for much of the dollars spent. Customers also came back. Among Cash App users who paid with bitcoin at least twice at the same merchant, the median was three purchases per customer-merchant pair. About 44% of bitcoin payments from Cash App were repeat payments, and 86% of those came within 30 days. The activity was not limited to Block’s own app. External Lightning wallets such as Strike, Wallet of Satoshi, Phoenix and Coinbase handled 56.6% of Square bitcoin payments and about 66% of payment value, while Cash App wallets made up the rest. Square sellers can choose how much of each sale they keep in bitcoin, and Square converts the rest to dollars automatically. Block said zero-fee processing for bitcoin payments on Square has been extended through Dec. 31, 2027. Local governments are testing similar setups, with Miami-Dade County now taking bitcoin for property taxes and converting it to dollars. A push for a de minimis bitcoin exemption Block tied the data to tax policy. Under current U.S. federal rules, paying with bitcoin generally means calculating a capital gain or loss on every purchase, even a $10 coffee, the company said. A Morning Consult survey that Block commissioned found that 23.6% of businesses that don’t accept bitcoin cite tax and accounting complexity as a reason. That is about the same share that cite regulation, refunds or price swings. Among businesses that have considered taking bitcoin but haven’t, the figure was 27%. Consumers pointed to friction, too. business.title: Bitcoin Hovers Just Above Average Holder’s Cost Basis as Price Keeps Dipping
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Hovers Just Above Average Holder’s Cost Basis as Price Keeps Dipping Bitcoin is trading just above its realized price, the average cost of every coin on the network, and a break below that level would put the average holder at a loss for the first time since early 2023, Glassnode, an onchain analytics firm posted Friday. The price of bitcoin sat near $61,700 on Friday after sliding below $62,000. The realized price is a measure of what holders paid, not where the market trades. When bitcoin trades above it, the typical coin is sitting on a gain. Below it, the typical coin is underwater. The margin is thin. The firm said the MVRV ratio, which compares bitcoin’s market value with its realized value, sits “just above 1.” A reading of 1 means the market price has fallen all the way to the realized price. What the realized price measures Realized price values each coin at the price it last moved on the blockchain, then averages across the supply. Look Into Bitcoin describes it as bitcoin’s average cost basis. Because it tracks the price when coins last changed hands, it moves far more slowly than the market. The MVRV ratio expresses the same idea as a multiple. Above 1, holders are in profit on average. Below 1, they are not. A reading just above 1 means the market price is only a sliver higher than what the average coin cost. The firm did not give the exact realized price in its post, which included a chart. That leaves the exact cushion between today’s price and the average cost basis unstated. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Slips Near $61,500 as Tech Selloff Spreads to Asia The bitcoin price slipped to near $61,500 on Friday morning, according to Look Into Bitcoin data, as a selloff in technology stocks that followed Anthropic’s Nasdaq debut spread to Asian markets and dragged bitcoin to its lowest level since July. Bitcoin first broke below $62,000 on Thursday evening, after Thursday afternoon’s report showed it giving back a rebound toward $64,000. The bitcoin price then slid to nearly $61,200 during Asian trading before bouncing back above $61,700. Friday marks a third straight day of losses. Asian stocks extend the AI rout The selling started in Asia. South Korea’s Kospi slid more than 5%, with chipmakers SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics down around 6%. The Korea Exchange halted program selling for five minutes after the drop, while Japan’s Nikkei fell as much as 4.85% to a seven-month low. U.S. futures pointed lower too. Nasdaq-100 futures fell more than 1.7% and S&P 500 futures dropped 0.8%, Yahoo Finance reported. Gold futures lost 3%. The S&P 500 is pointing to a seventh straight daily decline, its longest losing streak since the start of the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020. Anthropic shares fell 8% in premarket trading after closing their first session at $97.17, up 17% from the $83 IPO price. Nvidia was down about 2.4% and AMD fell nearly 7%, CNBC reported. Hawkish signals from Federal Reserve officials this week also weighed on sentiment, Reuters said. ETF outflows and liquidations pressure the bitcoin price Bitcoin funds are feeling the pressure. BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) recorded $541.1 million in net outflows on Thursday, its largest single-day outflow since launch. entertainment.description: Chef Soliat Bada Anyone who grew up in a Nigerian home knows the line. You suggest buying food outside, and before you finish the sentence, someone reminds you that there’s rice at home. It is usually the end of the conversation. In Asali Africa’s new series, it is where the conversation starts. There’s Rice at Home is a cooking and conversation show from Asali Africa, the Lagos-based creative development agency, hosted by Chef Soliat Bada . In each episode, Soliat cooks one rice dish with a guest, and while the pot does its work, the two get into the kind of talk that usually happens around food: family, money and what success really looks like. Rice is the most ordinary thing in a Nigerian kitchen, and the show makes a good case that it doesn’t have to taste ordinary. Over five episodes, released every two weeks, the menu travels from Jamaica to Saudi Arabia, back home to Nigeria and on to Louisiana. You don’t just watch the food get made, either. The season opens with Rice and Peas with Oxtail, the Jamaican Sunday staple of rice cooked in coconut milk with red kidney beans (the “peas”), served beside rich, slow-cooked oxtail. Soliat’s guest is Michael Famoroti , co-founder of Stears, and their conversation turns to family and black tax: the expectation that once you start earning, you start supporting the people who raised you. He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. Frequent questions men are asked: “How far? Work nko?” “When are you getting married?” “Have you bought land?” “How is the family?” And the famous Nigerian question that can make an unemployed graduate dread family gatherings: “So, what are you doing now?” We often inquire about their achievements, responsibilities, and plans. These aspects are important, but how often do we ask about their fears? A father who leaves home before sunrise and returns exhausted, burdened by the weight of school fees, rent, and family expectations. A young graduate who has submitted countless job applications, yet still smiles politely when another relative inquires why he hasn’t found a job. A successful professional whose LinkedIn profile showcases numerous achievements, while his personal life tells a story that no one has thought to ask about. We admire their strength, we applaud their sacrifices, and we celebrate their accomplishments. But what about what they are going through? The person everyone leans on also needs somewhere to lean. Society has an interesting checklist for measuring a man’s success. A good job, a house, a car, a wife, children and financial stability. Preferably, all achieved before a certain age. I lost someone recently, and since then, I have found myself revisiting little moments, conversations and encounters I probably would not have given much thought to otherwise. We weren’t particularly close , or I wouldn’t describe our relationship that way . We had reconnected after a long time and started seeing each other more often, especially after I resumed work following an accident I was involved in. He gradually became part of my daily routine. Whenever I went to work, he would come to pick me up from the office, and we would go home together. In many ways, he looked out for me and made sure I got home safely. We started talking more. We would discuss life, share experiences and occasionally open up about things happening in our individual lives. There was also an emotional dimension to our friendship. He was interested in me romantically, I realised, but I didn’t feel the same way. I tried to understand my feelings, but the truth was that I simply wasn’t in love with him. I couldn’t manufacture feelings that weren’t there. Then I heard that he passed away. My first reaction, strangely, was guilt. I began asking myself: Was I a good friend to him? Was I kind enough? Was I considerate? Did I treat him well? Could I have done something differently? I caught myself wondering whether I should have given him a chance . Perhaps I should have allowed him to love me. But then would I have done that out of genuine affection or simply out of pity? And would that have been fair to either of us? My understanding is that not returning someone’s romantic feelings does not mean we cannot offer them genuine friendship, kindness and compassion. I didn’t owe him romantic love, but I could have been a good friend. That has stayed with me. Beyond the guilt, there was another question I couldn’t get out of my head: Why did God allow us to reconnect? Why, after such a long time, did our paths have to cross again? Why did we have to start talking, sharing experiences and becoming familiar with each other again, only for him to die shortly afterwards? Why him? Why at that particular time?
